To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the contractile force of frog myocardial strip stimulated by impulses of low frequency was diminished to 2--5% of initial value when perfusing with Ringer's solutions containing 2.4 mM Mn2+, while the amplitude of contractile force was increased to 30% of initial value in the presence of 2 X 10(-4) g/ml ouabain.
the contractile force of a myocardial strip of frog ventricle is diminished when perfused with manganese-containing Ringer's solution.
contracture of the myocardium was observed in frog ventricles perfused by Ringer's solution with manganese ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the calcium transport in the contractile mechanism of frog ventricle.
the possibility of the development of contractures in the frog myocardium under the conditions of calcium channel blocking by manganese ions.
the mechanism of the development of contractures of the frog ventricular muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium ions are the only source for the contracture of the myocardium.
the contracture observed in this study was not a result of the increase of intracellular calcium ions, but of nonelectrogenic influx of calcium ions into the muscle fibers.
contracture is a phenomenon of nonelectrogenic transport of calcium ions into the myocardial fibers, which is not blocked by manganese ions, while it is blocked by lanthanum ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
contracture is a phenomenon which can be produced by different mechanisms, and it is possible to differentiate them by using manganese or lanthanum ions.
the calcium channels are not the only source of calcium for the myocardium.
the calcium channels play a significant role in the regulation of contractility of the frog heart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
manganese ions can be used as an effective tool for the study of the mechanisms of calcium transport in the heart muscle.
manganese can be used to study the role of calcium ions in the contractility of the heart muscle.
the contracture of frog heart muscle fibers can be induced in the presence of a calcium channel blocker.
